signature: A Perplexed Idempotent, of Rees Matrix Terrace
subject: On squaring
body: Sir, whenever I am squared I come back exactly as I was, so that $e^2 = e$. My friends call this stability. My mother calls it stubbornness.
Which of them is right? I should like to know before the family reunion.
reply: Madam, both. In semigroup theory these are the same virtue.

signature: A Worried Zero, of Absorbing Lane
subject: Attention at last
body: Sir, everything I multiply becomes me. I did not ask for this. Guests arrive as themselves and leave as zero, and I am beginning to feel the party depends on nobody noticing.
Is it too late to become the identity?
reply: Madam, the identity makes friends and you keep them. Both are respectable roles.

signature: An Inverse, Seeking My Other Half
subject: A question of uniqueness
body: Sir, I was told that in an inverse semigroup each element has exactly one inverse. I find this romantic, and also a little limiting.
Do other kinds of semigroups allow more options?
reply: Madam, regular semigroups do. Whether more options means more happiness we leave to the correspondence columns.

signature: A Weary Generator
subject: Sole responsibility
body: Sir, I generate everyone in this semigroup by myself. Every element is a power of me, and no one has once said thank you.
Is this what it means to be cyclic?
reply: Sir, yes. You may take comfort that the structure has a very short family tree.

signature: A Non-Commuting Couple, of Left Bank
subject: Does order matter?
body: Sir, when my partner and I walk in, I go first and he follows, and the result is $ab$. When he goes first it is $ba$, and the results differ.
We wish to know whether to stop fighting about doors.
reply: Madam, order matters. Please settle it by agreement, as the associative law allows you to regroup but not to reorder.

signature: A Finite Basis Sceptic
subject: Too many identities
body: Sir, I am told that some semigroups satisfy infinitely many identities that cannot all be reduced to a finite list.
I find this suspicious. Surely someone could have written them down by now?
reply: Sir, some have been proved to resist it. Writing them down is a longer task than one expects.

signature: A Nilpotent, Feeling Powerless
subject: Running out of strength
body: Sir, I am told that some power of me is zero. I do not know which power, and I do not wish to find out.
How should one prepare?
reply: Sir, with a calendar. It is the index of nilpotency, and it is finite.

signature: An Ideal Reader, of Two-Sided Crescent
subject: On being absorbed
body: Sir, I am an ideal, and anything that touches me stays inside. Visitors say it is charming, and also that it is difficult to leave.
Am I too welcoming?
reply: Madam, no. Closure under outside influence is the whole point of your profession.

signature: A Frobenius Coin Collector
subject: A shortage of change
body: Sir, I carry only coins worth 3 and 5. Shopkeepers keep telling me the exact amount I cannot pay.
What is the largest sum I can never make?
reply: Sir, seven. For coprime coins the largest is $ab - a - b$, and $3 \cdot 5 - 3 - 5 = 7$.

signature: A Monoid, Missing Her Identity
subject: Lost and found
body: Sir, I was a semigroup until someone adjoined an identity to me, and I now have a number to be returned to when everyone forgets who I am.
Is this progress?
reply: Madam, it is a monoid, and yes, it is progress. Please remember to bring it to the reunion.

signature: A Band, Rather Square
subject: Everything the same
body: Sir, every element of my family satisfies $x^2 = x$. Visitors find us repetitive.
We prefer to call it consistent. May we hope for your support?
reply: Sirs, you have it. Consistency is idempotent, and so is this reply.

signature: A Reader Troubled by Green
subject: Too many relations
body: Sir, I am told that Green has several relations, and I cannot keep track of whom to invite.
How many should I expect at dinner?
reply: Madam, five, namely $\mathcal{R}$, $\mathcal{L}$, $\mathcal{H}$, $\mathcal{D}$ and $\mathcal{J}$. Seat the $\mathcal{H}$ by the window.

signature: A Subsemigroup in Distress
subject: Closed but lonely
body: Sir, I am closed under multiplication, and nobody invites me out. They say I keep to myself.
Could they be right?
reply: Sir, they are correct but unfair. Self-containment is a compliment among subsemigroups.

signature: A Grateful Student of Cayley
subject: On embeddings
body: Sir, I have been told that every group sits inside a group of permutations, and that semigroups have a similar rule.
I find this reassuring. It means nobody is truly abstract.
reply: Sir, quite so. Every structure here is secretly a set of maps in disguise.

signature: A Caffeinated Commutator, of Espresso Row
subject: On morning efficiency
body: Sir, I commute only after my first coffee, and the second makes me nilpotent.
Is this a normal pattern for a working mathematician?
reply: Sir, it is the usual one. The market price of the beans is printed a few columns away.

signature: An Unrelated Element, of Concatenation Close
subject: On being free
body: Sir, I am told that I am the free semigroup on two letters, and that my elements are simply the finite words, joined end to end.
I have no relations to my name, except that brackets do not matter. Is this freedom, or only loneliness?
reply: Freedom, sir. Every map from your letters into any semigroup extends to a homomorphism in exactly one way. Few of us can say as much for our relatives.

signature: A Restless Congruence, of Compatible Row
subject: Not quite a normal subgroup
body: Sir, in group theory my cousin the normal subgroup does all the quotienting. I am told that in a semigroup that is not enough, and that it takes someone like me.
Is it true that I am an equivalence that survives multiplication on either side?
reply: It is true: an equivalence relation where $a \sim b$ implies $ca \sim cb$ and $ac \sim bc$. Quotients follow naturally.

signature: A Reluctant Ideal, of Quotient Lane
subject: Asked to collapse
body: Sir, I am an ideal, and I have been asked to collapse to a single point so that the rest of the semigroup may carry on around me.
I am told this is called a Rees quotient. Does the rest of the semigroup at least remember me?
reply: It does. You become the zero, and every other element keeps its identity. Few collapses are so tidy.

signature: A Forgetful Left Zero, of First Street
subject: On remembering
body: Sir, whenever I am multiplied, $xy = x$. I always remember the first and forget the second.
My neighbour on Second Street says the opposite. Are we related?
reply: Closely: he is the right zero semigroup, your opposite. Both are bands, and neither is commutative once there are two elements.

signature: A Meet-Minded Semilattice, of Lower Bound Mews
subject: Commutative and idempotent
body: Sir, I satisfy $xy = yx$ and $xx = x$, and my friends say I am nothing but a meet.
Is that all there is to me?
reply: Very nearly. A commutative band is the same thing as a meet semilattice, with $xy$ as the greatest lower bound. It is a distinguished life.

signature: A Cautious Cyclist, of Index Road
subject: A monogenic puzzle
body: Sir, I am generated by one element $a$, and I am told that $a^4 = a^6$ while no earlier powers coincide.
How many elements do I have?
reply: Five: $a, a^2, a^3, a^4, a^5$. The tail $a, a^2, a^3$ never returns, while $a^4$ and $a^5$ circle forever.

signature: A Partial Bijection, of Domain Drive
subject: Permission to be undefined
body: Sir, I am a bijection between one subset of a set and another, and I am not defined elsewhere.
A certain society says I may not be a permutation. May I still belong to something?
reply: You are welcome in the symmetric inverse monoid, where partial bijections multiply by composing wherever possible. Every inverse semigroup embeds there.

signature: A Counting Transformation, of Full Monoid Row
subject: How many of us?
body: Sir, I am a map from $\{1, 2, 3\}$ to itself, with no other requirements. A rumour says there are 27 of us.
Is the rumour true?
reply: It is: $3^3 = 27$, and in general $n^n$ for $n$ points. You live in the full transformation monoid, where every semigroup finds a home.

signature: A Closed Class, of Pseudovariety Place
subject: Why only finite products?
body: Sir, I belong to a class of finite semigroups closed under homomorphic images, subsemigroups and finite products.
A variety may take arbitrary products, but I am told I must not. Why?
reply: Because an infinite product of finite semigroups is generally infinite, and you would leave the class. Hence pseudovariety, and Eilenberg's bridge to automata.

signature: An Undecided Pair of Words, of Relation Row
subject: A long wait
body: Sir, we are two words in a finitely presented semigroup, and we simply wish to know whether we are equal.
We have waited since 1947.
reply: Alas, no single procedure answers for every such presentation, as Markov and Post showed in 1947. Individual presentations can be kinder.

signature: A Lonely Magma, of Unbracketed Lane
subject: An operation without a rule
body: Sir, I have a binary operation and nothing else, and when I bracket $(xy)z$ and $x(yz)$ I may get different answers.
I do not think the semigroups will have me.
reply: You are a magma, and you are most welcome, though you are not a semigroup. Associativity is the single rule that admits you to ours.

signature: An Idempotent in Waiting, of Finite Close
subject: Will my powers ever settle?
body: Sir, I am an element of a finite semigroup, and I worry that my powers $a, a^2, a^3, \dots$ will go on forever without settling down.
Shall I ever find peace?
reply: You shall. Some power $a^n$ is idempotent, so $a^{2n} = a^n$. A finite semigroup cannot keep you wandering.

signature: A Matrix Unit, of Brandt Crescent
subject: Vanishing on contact
body: Sir, I am $e_{ij}$ in a Brandt semigroup. Whenever I meet an $e_{kl}$ with $j \neq k$, I vanish into the zero.
Is this a failing of character?
reply: Not at all. The product $e_{ij}e_{kl}$ is $e_{il}$ when $j = k$ and $0$ otherwise. You compose when you fit, as arrows do.

signature: An Opposite Number, of Mirror Row
subject: Everything backwards
body: Sir, I am told I am the opposite of a certain semigroup, in which $x \circ y$ means $yx$.
Am I the same as it, or only its reflection?
reply: Often only its reflection. Left zero and right zero semigroups are opposites, and for two or more elements they are not isomorphic.

signature: A Very Patient Reader, of Postal Row
subject: Where is my correspondence?
body: Sir, for three days I have checked the morning post and found nothing addressed to me.
Is the postal service associative, or have the letters simply been regrouped?
reply: The editor apologises. The post is now delivered daily and, in the spirit of $(ab)c = a(bc)$, regrouping never loses a letter.
